subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a split public-exposure pattern where browser/operator surfaces stay behind SSO/OIDC but mobile pairing uses a separate public `wss://` hostname protected by OpenClaw token plus device bootstrap auth?
rationale: The remaining request changes public security guidance for Gateway exposure and mobile bootstrap authentication, so automation should not define the supported trust boundary by itself.

options.title: Document split-host mobile pairing
options.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps browser/admin traffic behind identity-aware proxy auth while allowing a dedicated mobile `wss://` pairing host to use OpenClaw-native bootstrap auth.

options.title: Keep Tailscale Serve as the only documented default
options.body: Leave public `wss://` split-host deployments as unsupported advanced operator territory and only document Tailscale Serve plus existing reverse-proxy guidance.

options.title: Defer until release proof
options.body: Wait for the QR/onboarding fixes to ship and be retested before deciding whether the advanced public recipe should be documented.

recommendation.title: Document split-host mobile pairing
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps browser/admin traffic behind identity-aware proxy auth while allowing a dedicated mobile `wss://` pairing host to use OpenClaw-native bootstrap auth.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent route-list fix and adjacent pairing/security documentation work make this the best available owner for the remaining security-boundary decision.
